# Import notes — `dead-ends`

- **Source:** <https://github.com/AxiomMath/dead-ends> (paper: arXiv:2602.05095,
  "Dead ends in square-free digit walks"). Initial Lean code generated by
  [Axiom Math](https://axiommath.ai).
- **License:** the upstream repository is MIT-licensed (`Copyright (c) 2026 Axiom
  Math`). MIT is compatible with Lean Pool's Apache-2.0; the vendored files carry
  the Lean Pool Apache-2.0 header with the upstream maintainers credited as
  authors, and the MIT origin is recorded here and in the project card.
- **What was vendored:** only `Deadends/solution.lean`, copied to
  `LeanPool/DeadEnds/Solution.lean`. The upstream `Deadends/problem.lean` is the
  formal *problem statement* with deliberate `sorry` placeholders; it is fully
  subsumed by `solution.lean` (which restates every definition and proves every
  statement), so it is not vendored. No file with `sorry`/`admit`, a new
  `axiom`/`constant`, or `unsafe`/`partial`/`opaque`/`@[extern]` was imported.
- **Transformations applied:**
  - Prepended the Lean Pool four-line file header.
  - Stripped the upstream "proof generation time" comment banner.
  - Wrapped all declarations in `namespace LeanPool.DeadEnds … end
    LeanPool.DeadEnds` (upstream put everything at the top level; the wrapper
    avoids clashes between generic names like `error_bound` and other projects).
  - Replaced the broad `import Mathlib` with the specific Mathlib modules used.
  - Added module/declaration docstrings where the linter required them.
- **Toolchain bump:** ported from Lean `v4.26.0` (Mathlib `v4.26.0`) to Lean
  Pool's `v4.30.0-rc2`.
